en.title: Steam Surges Past $15 Billion in 2026, Fueled by Blockbuster Sequels
en.summary: Valve's PC storefront has already raked in an astounding $15 billion this year, with a handful of major releases driving its success. Analysts point to a strong reliance on established franchises for this massive revenue.
en.body:
## Steam's Monumental 2026 Performance

Valve's digital storefront, **Steam**, has once again proven its dominance in the PC gaming market, generating an incredible **$15 billion in revenue** by September 2026. This figure, according to Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics, has already surpassed the platform's total earnings for the entirety of 2023, signaling a potentially record-breaking year. The impressive haul is significantly bolstered by a select group of six games released this year, which collectively contributed nearly $1 billion to Valve's coffers.

Leading the charge among these top performers is **Forza Horizon 6**, which has revved up over **$210.5 million** since its launch. Hot on its heels are **Crimson Desert** and **Resident Evil Requiem**, securing second and third place with **$203.3 million** and **$200.9 million**, respectively. The enduring appeal of established series is further demonstrated by **Slay the Spire 2** ($148.4 million) and **Subnautica 2** ($139.2 million), both significant revenue generators. Even the more niche **Meccha Chameleon** managed to pull in **$89.8 million**.

## The Power of Established IPs

A key takeaway from Elliott's analysis is the significant role established franchises play in Steam's financial success. Out of the top six revenue-generating games this year, only two – **Crimson Desert** and **Meccha Chameleon** – represent new intellectual properties. The remaining four are direct sequels to games that already commanded substantial fanbases, underscoring a trend where players gravitate towards familiar, trusted titles.

This reliance on sequels is further emphasized when looking at the top 100 best-selling games released in 2026. While these games collectively generated approximately $2.4 billion, accounting for 15.9% of Steam's overall revenue so far, established IPs dominated the earnings. Of the new-game top 100, 63% were new IPs, but a staggering 52.5% of the revenue, or $1.25 billion, came from established franchises. **Crimson Desert**, despite being a new IP, is a standout success, accounting for roughly 18% of all revenue generated by new IPs within that top 100 list. This highlights that while new IPs can succeed, they often need to achieve remarkable traction to compete with the financial might of sequels.

## What's Next

With the year's end approaching and several high-profile releases still on the horizon, analysts predict **Steam** could exceed **$20 billion** in total revenue for 2026. This continued growth suggests a robust market for PC gaming, driven by both passionate fanbases and the consistent appeal of well-loved game series.

content_raw: 2026 has already shaped up to be an incredibly successful year for Valve. According to Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics, the company has managed to bring in $15 billion in revenue through Steam, with 6.6 percent of this revenue (approximately just under $1 billion) being attributed to six games that came out this year – Forza Horizon 6 , Crimson Desert , Resident Evil Requiem , Slay the Spire 2 , Subnautica 2 , and Meccha Chameleon . Forza Horizon 6 is leading the pack, having generated $210.5 million since its release. Crimson Desert is in second place with $203.3 million, and Resident Evil Requiem is in third place with $200.9 million. Slay the Spire 2 brought in $148.4 million in revenue for Steam, followed by Subnautica 2 generating $139.2 million, and Meccha Chameleon making $89.8 million. As Elliott points out in his social media post, of the top six revenue generators for Steam in 2026, only two are new IPs – Crimson Desert and Meccha Chameleon . The rest are sequels to games that had already been quite popular. Elliott has gone on to note that Crimson Desert on its own accounts for 18 percent of all revenue generated by new IPs in the top 100 best-selling games on Steam. The top 100 have made around $2.4 billion so far, contributing to 15.9 percent of overall Steam revenue. “The top 100 new 2026 games by gross revenue this year is about $2.4B, or about 15.9% of 2026’s Steam overall revenues so far. Of the new-game top 100, 63% were actually new IP, but 52.5% of the revenue ($1.25B) came from established IP. “But it’s worth noting Crimson Desert , with its $203M, accounts for about 18% of all new-IP revenue in the top 100. When we take Crimson out of the analysis, the 62 new-IP games make up only about 39%. So yeah, a lot of established IP is doing the legwork, as you’d expect.” It is also worth noting that two of the top six games – Slay the Spire 2 and Subnautica 2 – are still in Early Access, and as such, will likely see more sales further down the line as the games get updated with more content and polish. Forza Horizon 6 , Meccha Chameleon , and Crimson Desert , despite being full releases, also likely benefit from the fact that they see frequent updates, with developers adding in more content and fixing potential bugs. Resident Evil Requiem serves as the interesting outlier, since it is a single-player story-centric survival horror game. The sheer level of positive critical reception has likely played a major role in the title’s commercial success. Capcom even confirmed back in July that more than 8 million copies of the title had been sold across PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2. However, the company didn’t reveal more details about its sales on each platform. For more details on these titles, check out our reviews for Resident Evil Requiem , Crimson Desert , Subnautica 2 , and Forza Horizon 6 .
